{{Short description|Romanian philosopher (1920–2002)}}
[[File:Henri Wald in 1978.png|thumb|upright=1.2|Wald in 1978]]
'''Henri "Ricu" Wald''' (October 31, 1920{{spaced ndash}}July 14, 2002),<ref name="interview">{{cite web|url=http://net7.com/rjh/?page_id=661|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140118115511/http://net7.com/rjh/?page_id=661|url-status=dead|archive-date=2014-01-18|title=Henry Wald – 80|publisher=Romanian Jewish Heritage|date=Sep 2000|accessdate=2019-04-28}}</ref> also known as '''Henry Wald''',<ref name="interview"/> was a Romanian [[professor]], [[philosopher]], [[logic]]ian, and [[essayist]].<ref name = "yivo">{{cite web|url=http://www.yivoencyclopedia.org/article.aspx/Wald_Henri |title=Wald, Henri|publisher=[[The YIVO Encyclopedia of Jews in Eastern Europe]]|date= |accessdate=2018-07-02}}</ref>

==Early life==
Wald was born to a family of small merchants in [[Bucharest]], the capital of [[Romania]].<ref name = "yivo"/> Wald first became interested in [[philosophy]] at age sixteen, during a lecture given by one of his teachers.<ref name="interview"/> He was forced to leave high school in 1940 due to discriminatory [[anti-Jewish]] laws.<ref name = "yivo"/> Thus, Wald studied at a private college for Jewish students.<ref name = "yivo"/>

==Career==
During [[World War II]], Wald served in a forced labor detachment due to him being [[Jewish]].<ref name = "yivo"/> In terms of his political views, Wald was a [[Communist]] and "a radical [[Anti-fascism|antifascist]]".<ref name = "yivo"/> Wald began publishing in September 1944 in the newspaper ''Tribuna poporului'' (The People's Tribune).<ref name = "yivo"/> In addition, he also contributed to several additional leftist periodicals and to some cultural publications as well.<ref name = "yivo"/> Wald graduated from the faculty of philosophy at the [[University of Bucharest]] in 1946, after writing a dissertation called “The Petty Bourgeois Mentality.”<ref name="interview"/><ref name = "yivo"/> Wald became a professor of [[philosophy]] in Bucharest in 1948, a job which he occupied until 1962 (when he was fired due to his opposition to the official "[[National communism in Romania|nationalist-communist]]" stance of the then-Romanian government).<ref name = "yivo"/> Wald worked in several other educational institutions as well until his retirement in 1983.<ref name = "yivo"/> Due to his political commitments, Wald also worked in the [[propaganda]] department for the [[Communist Romania]]n regime in the late 1940s and early 1950s.<ref name = "yivo"/> Later on in his life, Wald became significantly closer to Judaism, which he thought was a "matrix of humanist thinking".<ref name = "yivo"/> Late in his life, the [[Romanian Radio Broadcasting Company]]’s Center for Oral History (C.O.H.) conducted an interview with Wald where he talked about and discussed his life story.<ref name = "interview"/> Wald died in 2002, at the age of 80.<ref name = "yivo"/><ref name="interview "/>
